## OpenAPI

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/openapi#openapi


| Term              | Annotation Target | OpenAPI field                                                                  |
|-------------------|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `externalDocs`  | EntityContainer   | Links to external documentation that explain more about APIs are helpful to developers. |
| `Extensions` | EntityContainer   | To add the sap defined (`x-sap`) specification extensions. This annotation can an be used in root, entity and in function/action level.                                        |


This is an example of a CDS service annotated with the annotations above:

```cds
annotate SampleService with @(
    OpenAPI:{
        externalDocs: {
            description: 'API Guide',
            url        : 'https://help.sap.com/docs/product/sample.html'
        },
        Extensions: {
        ![compliance-level]: 'sap:base:v1'
      }
    }
);
```


## Frequently Asked Questions

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/openapi#faq


Examples for typical questions on how to fine-tune the generated OpenAPI descriptions.

### Suppress GET (list and by-key) on an entity set?

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/openapi#suppress-get-list-and-by-key-on-an-entity-set


To suppress both types of GET requests to an entity set, annotate it with

```json
"@Capabilities.ReadRestrictions": {
    "Readable": false
}
```

### Suppress GET (list) on an entity set?

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/openapi#suppress-get-list-on-an-entity-set


To suppress only GET list requests to an entity set and still allow GET by-key, annotate it with

```json
"@Capabilities.ReadRestrictions": {
    "Readable": false,
    "ReadByKeyRestrictions": {
        "Readable": true
    }
}
```


### Suppress GET (by-key) on an entity set?

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/openapi#suppress-get-by-key-on-an-entity-set


To suppress only GET by-key requests to an entity set and still allow GET list, annotate it with

```json
"@Capabilities.ReadRestrictions": {
    "ReadByKeyRestrictions": {
        "Readable": false
    }
}
```

# Publishing to AsyncAPI

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/asyncapi


You can convert events in CDS models to the [AsyncAPI specification](https://www.asyncapi.com), a widely adopted standard used to describe and document message-driven asynchronous APIs.

Install the plugin like so:

```sh
npm add -D @cap-js/asyncapi
```

## Usage from CLI

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/asyncapi#cli


Use the following command to convert all services in `srv/` and store the generated AsyncAPI documents in the `docs/` folder:

```sh
cds compile srv --service all -o docs --to asyncapi
```

For each service that is available in the `srv/` files, an AsyncAPI document with the service name is generated in the output folder.
If you want to generate one AsyncAPI document for all the services, you can use `--asyncapi:merged` flag:

```sh
cds compile srv --service all -o docs --to asyncapi --asyncapi:merged
```

## Programmatic Usage

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/asyncapi#programmatic


```js
const cds = require('@sap/cds')
const { compile } = require('@cap-js/asyncapi')

const csn = await cds.load(cds.env.folders.srv)
const doc = compile(csn)
```

## Importing AsyncAPI

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/asyncapi#import


Use `cds import` to convert an AsyncAPI document into a CDS service definition:

```sh
cds import --asyncapi ~/Downloads/BookStore_AsyncAPI.json
```

[Learn more about `cds.import`](../../tools/apis/cds-import#from-asyncapi){.learn-more}

## Presets

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/asyncapi#presets


Use presets to add configuration for the AsyncAPI export tooling.

::: code-group
```json [.cdsrc.json]
{
  "export": {
    "asyncapi": {
      "application_namespace": "sap.example"
      [...]
    }
  }
}
```
:::

| Term                    | Preset Target | AsyncAPI field                | Remarks                                                                                                                  |
|-------------------------|---------------|-------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `merged.title`          | Service       | info.title                    | Mandatory when `--asyncapi:merged` flag is given.<br> `title` from here is used in the generated AsyncAPI document.      |
| `merged.version`        | Service       | info.version                  | Mandatory when `--asyncapi:merged` flag is given.<br> `version` from here is used in the generated AsyncAPI document     |
| `merged.description`    | Service       | info.description              | Optional when `--asyncapi:merged` flag is given.<br> `description` from here is used in the generated AsyncAPI document. |
| `merged.short_text`     | Service       | x-sap-shortText               | Optional when `--asyncapi:merged` flag is given.<br> The value from here is used in the generated AsyncAPI document.     |
| `application_namespace` | Document      | x-sap-application-namespace   | Mandatory                                                                                                                |
| `event_spec_version`    | Event         | x-sap-event-spec-version      |                                                                                                                          |
| `event_source`          | Event         | x-sap-event-source            |                                                                                                                          |
| `event_source_params`   | Event         | x-sap-event-source-parameters |                                                                                                                          |
| `event_characteristics` | Event         | x-sap-event-characteristics   |                                                                                                                          |

## Annotations

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/asyncapi#annotations


Use annotations to add configuration for the AsyncAPI export tooling.

::: tip
Annotations will take precedence over [presets](#presets).
:::

| Term (`@AsyncAPI.`)    | Annotation Target | AsyncAPI field                | Remarks                                                                                                                 |
|------------------------|-------------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `Title`                | Service           | info.title                    | Mandatory                                                                                                               |
| `SchemaVersion`        | Service           | info.version                  | Mandatory                                                                                                               |
| `Description`          | Service           | info.description              |                                                                                                                         |
| `StateInfo`            | Service           | x-sap-stateInfo               |                                                                                                                         |
| `ShortText`            | Service           | x-sap-shortText               |                                                                                                                         |
| `EventSpecVersion`     | Event             | x-sap-event-spec-version      |                                                                                                                         |
| `EventSource`          | Event             | x-sap-event-source            |                                                                                                                         |
| `EventSourceParams`    | Event             | x-sap-event-source-parameters |                                                                                                                         |
| `EventCharacteristics` | Event             | x-sap-event-characteristics   |                                                                                                                         |
| `EventStateInfo`       | Event             | x-sap-stateInfo               |                                                                                                                         |
| `EventSchemaVersion`   | Event             | x-sap-event-version           |                                                                                                                         |
| `EventType`            | Event             |                               | Optional; The value from this annotation will be used to overwrite the default event type in the AsyncAPI document. |

For example:

```cds
@AsyncAPI.Title        : 'CatalogService Events'
@AsyncAPI.SchemaVersion: '1.0.0'
@AsyncAPI.Description  : 'Events emitted by the CatalogService.'
service CatalogService {

  @AsyncAPI.EventSpecVersion    : '2.0'
  @AsyncAPI.EventCharacteristics: {
    ![state-transfer]: 'full-after-image'
  }
  @AsyncAPI.EventSchemaVersion  : '1.0.0'
  event SampleEntity.Changed.v1 : projection on CatalogService.SampleEntity;
}
```

## Extensions

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/asyncapi#extensions


`@AsyncAPI.Extensions` can be used to provide arbitrary extensions.
If a specific annotation exists for a given extension, it takes precedence over the definition using @AsyncAPI.Extensions.
For example, if both `@AsyncAPI.ShortText` and `@AsyncAPI.Extensions: { ![sap-shortText]: 'baz' }` are provided, the value from `@AsyncAPI.ShortText` will override the one defined in @AsyncAPI.Extensions.

For example:

```cds
@AsyncAPI.Extensions: {
  ![foo-bar]: 'baz',
  ![sap-shortText]: 'Service Base 1'
}
service CatalogService {

  @AsyncAPI.Extensions: {
    ![sap-event-source]: '/{region}/sap.app.test'
  }
  event SampleEntity.Changed.v1 : projection on CatalogService.SampleEntity;
}
```

The `@AsyncAPI.Extensions` annotation can be applied at both the service level and the event level.

Since the AsyncAPI specification requires all extensions to be prefixed with `x-`, the compiler will automatically add this prefix. Therefore, do not include the `x-` prefix when specifying extensions in `@AsyncAPI.Extensions`.

### Behavior with `--merged` flag

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/asyncapi#behavior-with---merged-flag


When the `--merged` CLI flag is used:

- Extensions defined via `@AsyncAPI.Extensions` on `services` are **ignored**.
- Extensions defined via `@AsyncAPI.Extensions` on `events` remain effective and are applied as expected.

## Type Mapping

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/asyncapi#mapping


CDS Type to AsyncAPI Mapping

| CDS Type                               | AsyncAPI Supported Types                                                                            |
|----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `UUID`                                 | `{ "type": "string", "format": "uuid" }`                                                            |
| `Boolean`                              | `{ "type": "boolean" }`                                                                             |
| `Integer`                              | `{ "type": "integer" }`                                                                             |
| `Integer64`                            | `{ "type": "string", "format": "int64" }`                                                           |
| `Decimal`, `{precision, scale}`        | `{ "type": "string", "format": "decimal", "x-sap-precision": <precision>, "x-sap-scale": <scale> }` |
| `Decimal`, without scale               | `{ "type": "string", "format": "decimal", "x-sap-precision": <precision> }`                         |
| `Decimal`, without precision and scale | `{ "type": "string", "format": "decimal" }`                                                         |
| `Double`                               | `{ "type": "number" }`                                                                              |
| `Date`                                 | `{ "type": "string", "format": "date" }`                                                            |
| `Time`                                 | `{ "type": "string", "format": "partial-time" }`                                                    |
| `DateTime`                             | `{ "type": "string", "format": "date-time" }`                                                       |
| `Timestamp`                            | `{ "type": "string", "format": "date-time" }`                                                       |
| `String`, `{maxLength}`                | `{ "type": "string", "maxLength": length }`                                                         |
| `Binary`, `{maxLength}`                | `{ "type": "string", "maxLength": length }`                                                         |
| `LargeBinary`                          | `{ "type": "string" }`                                                                              |
| `LargeString`                          | `{ "type": "string" }`                                                                              |

# Embedded Analytics

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics


With SAP HANA Cloud and SAP Analytics Cloud {.subtitle}

Embedded analytics allows you to evaluate and analyze real-time business data directly in your SAP HANA-based CAP application, without having to replicate data to an external data warehouse.



## Introduction

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#introduction


Using CDS, you define a multidimensional [analytical model](#glossary) on top of the entities of your application's domain model.
Upon deployment to SAP HANA Cloud, the necessary runtime objects and metadata for
SAP HANA's built-in [analytical query](#glossary) engine (SAP HANA Multi-Dimensional Services or MDS) are automatically created.

CAP applications have a built-in endpoint for handling analytical queries using the _InA_ (Information Access) protocol,
to which clients like SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC) can connect.
Based on the analytical model, the analytical queries are then executed by the SAP HANA Multi-Dimensional Services (MDS).

To be able to consume data, the analytical engine needs a (multidimensional) analytical model.
This section explains how to define such an analytical model in CAP CDS.
The following examples are snippets taken from an
[analytical model](https://github.tools.sap/cap/sflight-ea/blob/main/srv/analytics-model.cds)
of the "Embedded Analytics" variant of the CAP SFlight sample application.

The structure of the analytical model resembles a star: in the center there's an
[analytical cube](#glossary) entity (called "cube" in the remainder of the document)
surrounded by and connected to various [dimension entities](#glossary).

The cube is the analytical interface entity and is visible in analytical clients.
Usually, it's a view or projection on top of a more basic entity of the CDS model.


## Install Plugins

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#install-plugins


Regardless of the runtime, be it Node.js or Java, the CDS Enterprise Analytics Plugin is responsible to build the runtime objects and metadata for MDS.

Add the plugin and install it by running:

```sh
npm add @sap/cds-analytics --save-dev
```

::: details The added dependency
::: code-group

```jsonc [package.json]
{
  // ...
  "devDependencies": {
    // ...
    "@sap/cds-analytics": "^1.0.1",
  },
}
```

:::

:::details When using extensibility in multitenant scenarios, ...
... you have to add the dependency to `@sap/cds-analytics` also to the _package.json_
in the _mtx/sidecar_ folder.
:::

To install the runtime plugin, add a dependency to the _package.json_ for Node.js or to the _pom.xml_ for a CAP Java application:

::: code-group
```sh [Node.js]
npm add @sap/cds-adapter-ina-js
```

```xml [Java (pom.xml)]
<dependencies>
  <dependency>
    <groupId>com.sap.firefly</groupId>
    <artifactId>cds-adapter-ina</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.3</version>
  </dependency>
  ...
</dependencies>
```
:::

This plugin provides the endpoint for handling InA requests.

::: tip Security Aspects
The plugin requires no further configuration but uses the security settings you added to your application. Also see [Add Authorization](#add-authorization).
:::

### Troubleshooting plugin installation and runtime issues

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#troubleshooting-plugin-installation-and-runtime-issues


#### Run locally before deploying to BTP

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#run-locally-before-deploying-to-btp


Verify that the application runs in your local development environment. Testing locally rules out authentication and routing issues. If the app works locally but fails after deployment to BTP, the problem is likely with the application's configuration (for example routing or CORS) rather than with the plugins.

#### 404 Not Found (local development environment and BTP)

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#404-not-found-local-development-environment-and-btp


When `GetServerInfo` request returns `Cannot GET /sap/bc/ina/service/v2/GetServerInfo` with status `404 Not Found`. Make sure the runtime plugin is properly installed.

#### 404 Not Found (BTP)

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#404-not-found-btp


If the `GetServerInfo` request succeeds locally but returns a 404 after deployment to BTP, verify the routing configuration in `xs-app.json` and ensure the InA service endpoints are exposed. See [Prepare for Production](#prepare-for-production) for details.

#### Authentication issues

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#authentication-issues


- Access errors
  Temporarily remove the `@restrict` and `@requires` annotations from the analytical model and run the application locally. If access succeeds, reintroduce the annotations incrementally to identify which rule causes the failure.
- No access to the data source in local development environment
  The CAP application running locally uses mock authentication that comes with pre-defined users. Their configuration may not be sufficient for the analytical model(s) used by your application. If a `GetResponse` request returns:

  ```json
  { "Messages": [ { "Number": 6037, "Text": "No access to the data source.", "Type": 2 } ] }
  ```

  Configure your own mock users. See [Explicitly Defined Mock Users](/@external/java/security#custom-mock-users) for Java and [Mocked Authentication](/@external/node.js/authentication#mocked) for Node.js.

- CORS errors
  If you access analytical models from a domain other than the CAP application (for example, SAP Analytics Cloud), add that domain to the CORS configuration in your `mta.yaml` or in the appropriate deployment descriptor. See [Prepare for Production](#prepare-for-production) for details.

#### Catalog request returns no models

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#catalog-request-returns-no-models


If an InA Catalog request succeeds but returns no models, the InA service is working but the analytical models were not deployed to HANA. This commonly happens when `@sap/cds-ea-plugin` is missing or installed from the wrong repository. Verify deployment by running:

```bash
cds deploy --to hana
```

and inspect the build output for generated .hdbcalculationview files (for example: `db/src/gen/*.hdbcalculationview`).

```shell
done > wrote output to:
   db/src/gen/.hdiconfig
   db/src/gen/.hdinamespace
   db/src/gen/@FLIGHTSERVICE_FLIGHTBYAIRPORT@CurrencyCode.hdbcalculationview
   ...
   db/src/gen/ALPService.TravelStatus_texts.hdbview
   ... 128 more. Run with DEBUG=build to show all files.
build completed in 1894 ms
```

## Declare an Analytical Service

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#declare-an-analytical-service


To expose a cube for consumption by InA clients, first declare an "analytical" service. This
is a service with protocol `ina`.

```cds
@protocol: 'ina'
service FlightService {
  // This is where you define your analytical service in the next step
  };
```

This service is then an interface, for example, for consumption by SAP Analytics Cloud.

>Add a screenshot of a dashboard build on this scenario.

## Define a Cube

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#define-a-cube


A cube represents the multidimensional model. It contains [analytical measures](#about-measures) and [dimension fields](#about-dimensions).

Inside the analytical service, define a minimalistic example cube:

```cds
@protocol: 'ina'
service FlightService {
  @ObjectModel.modelingPattern: #ANALYTICAL_CUBE
  @ObjectModel.supportedCapabilities: [#ANALYTICAL_PROVIDER]
  entity FlightByAirport as select from my.Flight {
    // This is where you add measures and dimensions to your Cube in the next steps
  }
};
```

A cube is characterized by an `entity` with the annotations `@ObjectModel.modelingPattern: #ANALYTICAL_CUBE` and `@ObjectModel.supportedCapabilities: [#ANALYTICAL_PROVIDER]`. In a cube entity, every element that is not defined as a measure is automatically a dimension. So the current cube doesn't have measures, which means that all fields of the `Flight` entity become dimensions for the `FlightByAirport` cube.

> The annotations used here are the same in ABAP, S4/HANA, and SAP Datasphere. If you'd like to see more convenience to make modelling easier in CAP, let us know.

::: warning No exposure via projection
Currently it is not possible to define a cube outside of an analytical service
and then expose it via a projection in the service.
:::


### Add Authorization

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#add-authorization


The [CDS authorization concept](/@external/guides/security/authorization) also applies to a cube entity.
Add respective annotations to the cube to define [restrictions](/@external/guides/security/authorization#restrictions)
(in the `where` condition for instance based authorization, [Exists predicates](/@external/guides/security/authorization#exists-predicate)
and [Association Paths](/@external/guides/security/authorization#association-paths) are not supported).

```cds
@restrict: [{ // role "analytics" can see everything [!code focus:8]
  grant: ['READ'],
  to: 'analytics'
}, {  // role "analytics-restricted" can see only flights related to the user's country
  grant: ['READ'],
  to: 'analytics-restricted',
  where: 'DepartureCountryCode = $user.country OR DestinationCountryCode = $user.country'
}]
@ObjectModel.modelingPattern: #ANALYTICAL_CUBE
@ObjectModel.supportedCapabilities: [#ANALYTICAL_PROVIDER]
entity FlightByAirport as select from my.Flight {
  //...
};
```

## About Measures

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#about-measures


Analytical measures (or simply measures) are elements of the cube that contain quantifiable data,
for example, the price of a flight, or the number of available seats for a flight. Measures must have a numeric data type.
The purpose of analytics is to gain an understanding of these numbers.
A cube must have at least one measure. All elements of the cube that are not marked as measure are
treated as [dimension fields](#define-dimensions).

Add annotation `@AnalyticsDetails.measureType` to an element of a cube to make it a measure.
The value of the annotation determines the kind of the measure:

- `#BASE` for a base measure

  A _base measure_ is a cube element with the [`@AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #BASE`](#add-base-measures) annotation.
  It's a simple measure and can be a simple projection of a field in the cube's data source, or an expression based on such fields and numeric literals.

- `#CALCULATION` for a calculated measure

  A _calculated measure_ is a cube element with the [`@AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #CALCULATION`](#add-calculated-measures) annotation.
  It's an expression based on other measures of the cube and on numeric literals.

- `#RESTRICTION` for a restricted measure

  A _restricted measure_ is a cube element with the [`@AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #RESTRICTION`](#add-restricted-measure) annotation. Use it to exclude certain values from the standard aggregation, that is, only apply the standard aggregation to a part of the actual result set.


## Add Base Measures

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#add-base-measures


When executing a query, the analytical engine first performs a standard aggregation for each base measure
over all dimensions that are not part of the respective drill-down.
The type of this aggregation is specified via the annotation `@Aggregation.default`
with possible values `#SUM, #MAX, #MIN, #AVG, #COUNT, #COUNT_DISTINCT`.
If no aggregation behavior is specified, `#SUM` is used.

In the case of an expression, this expression is evaluated _before_ the standard aggregation.

Example:

```cds
entity FlightByAirport as select from my.Flight {
  // ...
  @AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #BASE
  Price,
  @(AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #BASE)
  MaximumSeats,
  @(AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #BASE)
  OccupiedSeats,
  @(AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #BASE)
  @(Aggregation.default: #SUM)
  OccupiedSeats * Price as Profit : Decimal

  // ...
};
```

You learned that the default aggregation behavior is `#SUM`. So in the previous snippet you could also omit this annotation and have the same result. We added it here just for clarity.

> Note: Always add an explicit type, if you have an expression in the cube.

While the behavior of `#SUM`, `#MAX`, and `#MIN` is straightforward,
aggregation with `#AVG`, `#COUNT`, or `#COUNT_DISTINCT` need to be handled with care.
For data sources where the technical key and the semantic key are not the same,
naive usage of `#AVG`, `#COUNT`, or `#COUNT_DISTINCT` may lead to unexpected results. Those can be data sources containing delta-bookings or cancellations, or that contain the same record multiple times.
Use an [exception aggregation](#exception-aggregation) in such situations.

In SFlight we don't have these complications, so we can go with the standard aggregation.

For counting (with `#COUNT` or `#COUNT_DISTINCT`), the actual value of the referenced element
is ignored. Thus, it is recommended to always define a new element.


### Count Records

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#count-records


Use `#COUNT` if you simply want to show the number of flights:

```cds
entity FlightByAirport as select from my.Flight {
  // ...
  @AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #BASE
  @Aggregation.default: #COUNT
  1 as FlightCount : Integer,
  // ...
};
```


### Distinct Combinations

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#distinct-combinations


In a business context a plain `COUNT` usually is not very helpful.
Most often you would rather do a `#COUNT_DISTINCT`. Specify the dimensions whose
distinct values are to be counted via annotation `@Aggregation.referenceElement`.
The value of this annotation is an array where dimension fields and navigation attributes
can be provided.

Example: Get number of distinct combinations of `AirlineID` and `ConnectionID`.

```cds
entity FlightByAirport as select from my.Flight {
  // ...
  @AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #BASE
  @Aggregation.default: #COUNT_DISTINCT
  @Aggregation.referenceElement: [AirlineID, ConnectionID]
  1 as AirlineConnectionCount : Integer,
  // ...
};
```

The combination of `#COUNT_DISTINCT` and `@Aggregation.referenceElement` can be regarded
as a short-cut for an [exception aggregation](#exception-aggregation).

> TODO: **Why not move it to Exception Aggregation?**

### Average

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#average


You can use `#AVG` for doing simple averages, like the average number of occupied seats:

```cds
entity FlightByAirport as select from my.Flight {
  // ...
  @AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #BASE
  @Aggregation.default: #AVG
  OccupiedSeats as AvgOccSeats : Decimal,
  // ...
};
```

For more complicated averages, use [exception aggregation](#exception-aggregation),
or provide separate measures for the sum and the count and then compute
the average via a [Calculated Measure](#add-calculated-measures).



## Add Calculated Measures

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#add-calculated-measures



You cannot refer to elements of the cube's data source.
The expression is evaluated _after_ standard aggregation has been performed for the `#BASE` measures.

Example:

```cds
entity FlightByAirport as select from my.Flight {
  // ...
  @AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #BASE
  MaximumSeats,
  @AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #BASE
  OccupiedSeats,

  // calculated measure
  @AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #CALCULATION
  $self.MaximumSeats - $self.OccupiedSeats as AvailableSeats : Integer,
  // ...
};
```

Note:

- To address other measures in the expression for a calculated measure, prefix them with `$self`.
- Always add an explicit type if you have an expression in the cube.
- Annotation `@Aggregation.default` is irrelevant (ignored) for calculated measures.

See also: [List of supported operators and functions (internal link)](https://github.wdf.sap.corp/pages/orca/seal/seal-service/features/views/analyticalModel/calculations/ckf/).

When an expression contains an "unsuitable" combination of measures (like adding a measure without
currency to a measure with a currency), the analytical engine will evaluate the expression
and mark the result as "mixed", like for aggregating values with different currencies/units.





## Add Restricted Measure <Beta />

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#add-restricted-measure


The cube element must be a `CASE` expression with only one `WHEN`/`THEN` clause, `ELSE` is not allowed.
The `THEN` clause must contain a single reference to another measure of the cube,
expressions are not supported.

For computing a restricted measure, the result set is filtered according to
the `WHEN` condition before standard aggregation is applied.
This condition can use literals, dimension fields, and parameters of the cube.

Example:

```cds
entity FlightByAirport as select from my.Flight {
  // ...

  @AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #RESTRICTION
  case when $self.PlaneType = :PreferredPlaneType
    then $self.AvailableSeats
    end as AvailableSeatsOnPreferredPlaneType : Integer,

  // ...
};
```

Note: Annotation `@Aggregation.default` is irrelevant, like for Calculated Measures.

::: warning

Currently the behavior of Restricted Measures is different from what is documented here.
Either behavior or documentation will change.

:::



## Exception Aggregation <Beta />

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#exception-aggregation


An exception aggregation can be applied to any measure (base, calculated, or restricted).

Example: Use exception aggregation to count the number of distinct combinations
of `AirlineID` and `ConnectionID`:

```cds
entity FlightByAirport as select from my.Flight {
  // ...
  @AnalyticsDetails.exceptionAggregationSteps: [{
    exceptionAggregationBehavior: #SUM,
    exceptionAggregationElements: [AirlineID,ConnectionID]
  }]
  @AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #CALCULATION
  //@Aggregation.default: #NONE
  @Common.Label: null @title:null
  1 as ExcAggCount : Integer,
  // ...
};
```

Example: You compare flight prices from various airlines.
When looking at them on the granularity of single FlightDates, you want to see the minimum prices.
When FlightDate is not part of the drill-down at all, or when the granularity
is Month, Quarter, and so on, then you want to see the average over these minimum prices
for the respective time period.

For this, define a measure with exception aggregation.

```cds
entity FlightByAirport as select from my.Flight {
  // ...
  @AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #BASE
  @AnalyticsDetails.exceptionAggregationSteps: [{
    exceptionAggregationBehavior: #AVG,
    exceptionAggregationElements: [ FlightDate ]
  }]
  Price as AvgMinPrice,
  // ...
};
```

Supported values for `exceptionAggregationBehavior` are:

| Value           | Description |
| ---             | ---         |
| SUM             | Sum         |
| MIN             | Minimum     |
| MAX             | Maximum     |
| COUNT           | Count       |
| COUNTNULL       | Count, ignore data where value is NULL                |
| COUNTNULLZERO   | Count, ignore data where value is NULL or exactly 0   |
| AVG             | Average                                               |
| AVERAGENULL     | Average, ignore data where value is NULL              |
| AVERAGENULLZERO | Average, ignore data where value is NULL or exactly 0 |
| STD             | Standard deviation                                    |
| FIRST           | First entry w.r.t. ordering by dimension key values   |
| LAST            | Last entry w.r.t. ordering by dimension key values    |

This is how the system evaluates measures with exception aggregation:

1) Group by all dimensions that are not in the drill-down plus all `exceptionAggregationElements`.
2) Apply standard aggregation.
3) (if applicable) Perform a calculation for a calculated measure.
4) Apply specified exception aggregation along `exceptionAggregationElements`.

For more complicated cases several exception aggregation steps can be defined, which
are performed sequentially.

::: warning

Currently the behavior of Exception Aggregation is different from what is documented here.
Either behavior or documentation will change.

:::

## Currency and Unit

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#currency-and-unit


Measures can have a reference to a currency key or a unit key.
For a value with a currency (amount) or a value with a unit, connect the value field with the
currency or unit field via annotation:

```cds
@Measures.ISOCurrency: CurrencyCode_code
// or
@Measures.Unit: unit_code
```

In our flight example, `Price` has a currency:

```cds
entity FlightByAirport as select from my.Flight {
  // ...
  CurrencyCode,

  @AnalyticsDetails.measureType: #BASE
  @Measures.ISOCurrency: CurrencyCode_code //[!code ++]
  Price,
  // ...
};
```

::: tip No automatic currency or unit conversion is performed
If for such a measure values with different currencies (or units) are aggregated, the analytical engine aggregates the values regardless of their currency (or unit). The engine marks the result as "mixed" and it's up to the clients how to represent such a value.
:::


## About Dimensions

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#about-dimensions


_Dimension fields_, which are part of the cube, contain descriptive data, such as an airline ID or a flight date.
They provide the (business) context for the measures and are used for filtering and grouping the data.
Additional information for the dimension fields can be provided in corresponding dimension entities.

A _dimension entity_ is an entity with the annotations `@ObjectModel.modelingPattern: #ANALYTICAL_DIMENSION`
and `@ObjectModel.supportedCapabilities: [#ANALYTICAL_DIMENSION]`.
It provides additional attributes for a dimension field in the cube view.
Usually a dimension is a projection or view on top of a more basic entity in the model.

The connection between a dimension field in the cube and the corresponding dimension entity
is established via a `to-one` association from the cube to the dimension
and an annotation `@ObjectModel.foreignKey.association` at the dimension field that refers to this association.

## Define Dimensions

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#define-dimensions


Turn the Airline entity into a dimension and link it in the cube:

```cds
// dimension entity
annotate my.Airline with @ObjectModel.modelingPattern: #ANALYTICAL_DIMENSION //[!code ++]
                         @ObjectModel.supportedCapabilities: [#ANALYTICAL_DIMENSION]; //[!code ++]

entity FlightByAirport as select from my.Flight {
  @ObjectModel.foreignKey.association: to_Airline //[!code ++]
  AirlineID,
  to_Airline,  // association to the dimension entity //[!code ++]
  [...]
};
```

The attributes in a dimension can be used for

- Navigation Attributes
- Providing a text for a dimension field
- Defining a hierarchy


### Navigation Attribute

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#navigation-attribute


If you want to use an attribute of the dimension for grouping and/or filtering like
the dimension field, you have to add it to the cube. This way it becomes a "navigation attribute".
Analytical clients may show navigation attributes grouped below the dimension field.

A navigation attribute can also be an element of a dimension entity that is
not directly referenced in the cube but reached via another association.

Example:

```cds
entity FlightByAirport as select from my.Flight {
  // ...

  @ObjectModel.foreignKey.association: to_Connection
  ConnectionID,  // dimension field
  to_Connection,

  // navigation attributes
  to_Connection.DepartureAirport.AirportID as DepartureAirportID,
  to_Connection.DestinationAirport.AirportID as DestinationAirportID,

  // ...
};
```

:::tip New dimension
Adding a navigation attribute to the cube effectively adds a new dimension to the cube,
as one more characteristic is available for drill-down.
:::

### Texts

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#texts


Oftentimes you want to connect a dimension field or a navigation attribute with a text,
so that a client can display this text together with or instead of the dimension field's value.

To do so, add annotation `@ObjectModel.text.element` in the dimension entity.
The value of the annotation is a reference to the text field.

Example:

```cds
annotate my.Airline with
  @ObjectModel.modelingPattern: #ANALYTICAL_DIMENSION
  @ObjectModel.supportedCapabilities: [#ANALYTICAL_DIMENSION]
{
  @ObjectModel.text.element: Name
  AirlineID;
  @Semantics.text: true
  Name;
};
```

Now, analytical clients can show the airline name together with or instead of the ID,
even though the name is not an element of the cube.

### Localized Texts

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#localized-texts


If the text that you want to display is localized (based on CAP feature "localized data"),
do the following:

Add a projection on the respective `.texts` entity to your model, and add annotations
to declare it as a text entity. In the projection, you have to explicitly declare
the `locale` element as carrying the language code, and explicitly mark the
element that contains the actual text:

```cds
annotate sap.common.Countries.texts with
  @ObjectModel.modelingPattern: #LANGUAGE_DEPENDENT_TEXT
  @ObjectModel.supportedCapabilities: [#LANGUAGE_DEPENDENT_TEXT]
{
  @Semantics.language: true
  locale;
  @Semantics.text: true
  name;
};
```

In the dimension entity, use annotation `@ObjectModel.text.association` to connect
the `texts` association with the `code` field. If the dimension is a projection,
make sure that the `texts` association is projected.

```cds
annotate sap.common.Countries with
  @ObjectModel.modelingPattern: #ANALYTICAL_DIMENSION
  @ObjectModel.supportedCapabilities: [#ANALYTICAL_DIMENSION]
{
  @ObjectModel.text.association: texts
  code;
};
```

::: tip
Info: if an entity contains `localized` elements, the compiler automatically generates
a corresponding `.texts` entity and adds an association `texts` that points to the `.texts`
entity into the base entity. See also [Localized Data](/@external/guides/uis/localized-data).
:::



### Level-Based Hierarchies

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#level-based-hierarchies


A dimension can have a Level-Based Hierarchy to define hierarchical structures,
for example year, quarter, month, and date.
These hierarchies allow for roll-up and drill down of aggregated data,
for example January, February, and March can be rolled up as Q1.

First we define a base entity for holding calendar data.

```cds
entity CalendarDate {
  key Date: Date;
  Year: String(4);
  Halfyear: String(1);
  Quarter: String(1);
  Month: String(2);
};
```

::: tip
Note: You have to provide the data for this entity by yourself.
:::

Now we define a dimension entity for `FlightDate` as projection on
top of `CalendarDate` and make it a leveled hierarchy.
The calculated fields bring the values for `Quarter` and `Month` into
the format expected by SAC.

```cds
@ObjectModel.modelingPattern: #ANALYTICAL_DIMENSION
@ObjectModel.supportedCapabilities: [#ANALYTICAL_DIMENSION]
@Analytics.dimensionType: #TIME
@Hierarchy.leveled: [{
  name: 'YQMD',
  label: 'Year/Quarter/Month',
  levels: [{ element: Year }, { element: Quarter }, { element: Month }, { element: Date }]
}]
entity CalendarDateDimension as projection on CalendarDate {
  Date,
  @Common.IsCalendarYear: true
  Year,
  @Common.IsCalendarQuarter
  Year || Quarter as Quarter : String(5),
  @Common.IsCalendarMonth
  Year || (length(Month) = 1 ? '0' : '' ) || Month as Month : String(6)
};
```

Add an association to the new dimension in the Flight entity.

```cds
extend my.Flight with {
  to_FlightDate: Association[0..1] to CalendarDateDimension on to_FlightDate.Date = FlightDate;
};
```

In the cube, select the association and link it to dimension field `FlightDate`.
The elements of the hierarchy that shall be available for drill-down need to be
added as navigation attributes.

```cds
entity FlightByAirport as select from my.Flight {
  // ...
  @ObjectModel.foreignKey.association: to_FlightDate
  FlightDate,
  to_FlightDate,

  to_FlightDate.Month as FlightMonth,
  to_FlightDate.Quarter as FlightQuarter,
  to_FlightDate.Year as FlightYear,

  // ...
};
```

### Parent-Child Hierarchies

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#parent-child-hierarchies


Another type of hierarchy is a parent-child hierarchy.
We enhance our example by adding a dimension for plane types
that has a parent-child-hierarchy. In the base model there already is an entity for `PlaneType` that allows for
capturing a hierarchy:

```cds
entity sap.fe.cap.travel.PlaneType {
  key ID : String(10);
  Parent : String(10);
  // ... additional info
};
```

In the analytical model, we turn `PlaneType` into a dimension and
link it with the cube:

```cds
extend sap.fe.cap.travel.PlaneType with AnalyticalDimension;

extend my.Flight with {
  to_PlaneType: Association to PlaneType on to_PlaneType.ID = PlaneType;
};

entity FlightByAirport as select from my.Flight {
  // ...
    @ObjectModel.foreignKey.association: to_PlaneType
    PlaneType,
    to_PlaneType,

  // ...
};
```

Finally, we turn `PlaneType` into a parent-child hierarchy by adding the annotation
`@Hierarchy.parentChild`.
Property `recurse` defines the parent-child relation by linking respective elements of the entity.
In our example element `Parent` contains the ID of the parent entry.
The display order of siblings on the same hierarchy level can be defined via property `siblingsOrder`.

```cds
annotate sap.fe.cap.travel.PlaneType with @Hierarchy.parentChild: [{
  name: 'PlaneType',  // ID of the hierarchy
  label: 'Plane Types',
  recurse: {
      parent: [Parent],
      child: [ID]
  },
  siblingsOrder: [{
    by: ID,
    direction: 'DESC'
  }]
}];
```

For entities with a composite key, `recurse` and `siblingsOrder` allow to provide lists of elements.

In a client, leveled hierarchies and parent-child hierarchies behave the same.




## Prepare for Production

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#prepare-for-production

> Question: Or is that only a "Add SAP HANA Configuration" section, if we should decide to not elaborate too much on deployment? Otherwise we'd need to add more facets than just hana.

If not done already, add SAP HANA configuration to your project:

```sh
cds add hana,mta,xsuaa,approuter
```

This step is important to ensure that the `db/undeploy.json` file is available in your project and contains an entry for `hdbcalculationview` to undeploy possibly outdated artifacts.

Expose the route provided by the InA adapter through the approuter:

::: code-group

```js [app/router/xs-app.json]{2-6}
{"routes": [
        {
            "source": "^/sap/bc/ina/service/v2/(.*)$",
            "destination": "srv-api",
            "authenticationType": "xsuaa"
        }
     ]
     }
```
:::

Enhance the approuter module in the mta.yaml and replace `<your SAC tenant host url>`:

::: code-group
```yaml [mta.yaml]
- name: sflight
  [...]
  properties:
     CORS: '[{"uriPattern": "^/sap/bc/ina/(.*)$", "allowedOrigin":
       [{"host":"<your SAC tenant host url>",
       "protocol":"https"}], "allowedMethods": ["GET", "POST", "OPTIONS"],
       "allowedHeaders": ["Origin", "Accept", "X-Requested-With",
       "Content-Type", "Access-Control-Request-Method",
       "Access-Control-Request-Headers", "Authorization", "X-Sap-Cid",
       "X-Csrf-Token", "application-id"], "exposeHeaders": ["Accept",
       "Authorization", "X-Requested-With", "X-Sap-Cid",
       "Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "Access-Control-Allow-Credentials",
       "X-Csrf-Token", "Content-Type"]}]'
     COOKIES: '{"SameSite": "None"}'
     SESSION_TIMEOUT: 120
```
:::

## Glossary

> Source: /docs/guides/protocols/embedded-analytics#glossary


---

| **Term** | **Definition** |
| :------- | :------------: |
| Cube | A multidimensional model for analytics. |
| Measure | Quantifiable data in a cube. |
| Dimension | Descriptive data in a cube. |
| Base Measure | A simple measure in a cube. |
| Calculated Measure | A measure derived from other measures. |
| Restricted Measure | A measure with a filter applied before aggregation. |
| Exception Aggregation | Aggregation applied to a measure with specific conditions. |
| Analytical Service | A service with protocol `ina` for exposing analytical models. |
| Dimension Entity | An entity providing additional attributes for a dimension field. |
| Navigation Attribute | An attribute of a dimension used for grouping and filtering. |
| Hierarchy | A structure defining levels or parent-child relationships in dimensions. |
| Leveled Hierarchy | A hierarchy with predefined levels like year, quarter, month. |
| Parent-Child Hierarchy | A hierarchy where each element has a parent element. |
| Analytical Cube | The central entity in an analytical model containing measures and dimensions. |
| Analytical Model | A model defining the structure and relationships of data for analytics. |
| Analytical Query | A query executed by the analytical engine to retrieve data based on the model. |
| Analytical Plugin | A plugin responsible for creating runtime objects and metadata for analytics. |

# Native AI

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/


CAP provides intrinsic support for integrating native AI capabilities, including the use of MCP services, CAP-level Agents, and Vector Embeddings.
{.abstract}

[Model Context Protocol Adapter](./mcp.md)
: Turn your CAP services into an AI-powered solution by easily serving existing CAP services via MCP.

[CAP-level Agents](./agents.md)
: Learn how to utilize CAP-level Agents to automate tasks and integrate AI-driven workflows within CAP applications.

[Vector Embeddings](./embeddings.md)
: Learn how to leverage vector embeddings within CAP applications to enable advanced AI-driven search and recommendation capabilities.

# Model Context Protocol Adapter

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp


Simply annotate a CAP service with the [`@mcp`](#serving-mcp) annotation to expose it via [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/). With that it becomes accessible to AI agents and LLM-powered tools without additional implementation work.
{.abstract}

> [!caution] SAP API Policy Applies!
> The CAP MCP adapter is intended only for exposing _custom_ CAP application services. It is **_NOT_**{.red} an SAP-endorsed architecture or pathway for exposing, proxying, or providing agentic access to _SAP Application APIs_ as referred to in the [_SAP API Policy_](https://help.sap.com/doc/sap-api-policy), section 2.2.2. -> Read section [_SAP API Policy_](#sap-api-policy) below!


> [!note]
>
> This guide is about the *MCP Adapter* – for example, as provided through the [*@cap-js/mcp*](https://github.com/cap-js/mcp) plugin – which powers domain-specific application use cases, for example, to respond to questions for CAP-based applications like *"List all overstocked books"*.
>
> In parallel, there's also the *MCP Server* plugin ([*@cap-js/mcp-server*](https://github.com/cap-js/mcp-server)), which serves a different purpose, though, that is: AI-assisted *development* of CAP projects.



## Add the MCP Plugin

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#add-the-mcp-plugin



### In CAP Node.js Projects

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#in-cap-nodejs-projects


Within your project root run this to add the [`@cap-js/mcp`](https://github.com/cap-js/mcp) plugin:

```shell [Node.js]
npm add @cap-js/mcp
```
### In CAP Java Projects

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#in-cap-java-projects


Add the `cds-adapter-mcp` dependency to your `srv/pom.xml`:

::: code-group
```xml [srv/pom.xml]
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sap.cds</groupId>
  <artifactId>cds-adapter-mcp</artifactId>
  <scope>runtime</scope>
</dependency>
```
:::


## Declare `@mcp` Services

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#declare-mcp-services




### Using `@mcp` Annotation

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#using-mcp-annotation


Simply add the `@mcp` annotation to a service definition to expose it via MCP.  For example, add the following to `srv/cat-service.cds`:


::: code-group
```cds [srv/cat-service.cds]
// Serve via OData, HCQL and REST
annotate CatalogService with @odata @hcql @rest;
annotate CatalogService with @mcp; // [!code focus]
```
:::

You can also specify an alternative path under which the MCP endpoint should be served as usual with CAP protocol annotations:

```cds
annotate CatalogService with @mcp:'books'
```

> [!tip] Just Another Protocol
> From the perspective of a developer in a CAP-based project, `@mcp` is just another protocol for your services, similar to `@odata`, `@graphql`, `@rest`, or `@hcql`. The adapter takes care of the rest, with all the standard CAP features you know working out of the box also with MCP, including annotations like `@cds.query.limit`, etc.


### MCP-specific Services

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#mcp-specific-services


Frequently, you might want to create services that are tailored specifically for MCP usage.
Instead of annotating an existing service with `@mcp` and exposing all its entities and actions, simply create a dedicated service specifically for MCP. For example, you could create a `BooksService` that only exposes a subset of the entities of the `AdminService` like that:

::: code-group
```cds [srv/books-service.cds]
using { AdminService } from './admin-service';

@mcp service BooksService {

  @readonly entity Authors as projection on AdminService.Authors;
  @readonly entity Books as projection on AdminService.Books {
    ID, title, stock, price,
    author,
    genre.name as genre,
    currency.name as currency,
  }

  @requires: 'authenticated-user'
  action submitOrder ( book: Books:ID, quantity: Integer );
 }
```
:::


> => See also: [_Use Case-Oriented Services_](../../get-started/bookshop#use-case-specific-services) in the getting started guide.



### Providing Descriptions

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#providing-descriptions


As LLMs rely heavily on context information to create high-quality output, the adapter evaluates existing doc comments and annotations to provide additional information about the service, entities, elements, actions, and parameters to the LLM. This information is included in the output of the [`describe`](#-describe-service) tool and can be used by agents to better understand the data model and available actions/functions. In particular, the following information is evaluated:

- [Doc comments](../../cds/cdl#doc-comments) -> most recommended (Node.js only)
- `@title`
- `@description`

> [!note]
> Doc comments are only supported in Node.js. In Java, use `@title` and `@description` annotations instead.

For example, you can add doc comments to your entities and their elements like that:

```cds
/**
 * This is the author entity.
 * It contains information about book authors.
 */
annotate BookshopService.Authors with {
  /** The ID of the author. */
  ID;
  /** The name of the author. */
  name;
  /** The books written by the author. */
  books;
}
```



## Test-drive Locally

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#test-drive-locally


As usual, and following the Calesi principles of "convention over configuration", you can run your CAP server locally and interact with it using the MCP protocol from common clients like OpenCode or Claude Code.


### Run with `cds watch`

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#run-with-cds-watch


Run your CAP server locally as usual using `cds watch`, and note that the `@mcp`-annotated service gets served at an additional endpoint for the MCP protocol:

::: code-group
```shell [Node.js]
cds watch
```
```shell [Java]
mvn cds:watch
```
:::

```shell
[cds] - serving CatalogService {
  at: [ ..., '/mcp/browse' ],
  ...
}
```


### Using OpenCode, or alike

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#using-opencode-or-alike


Assumed you have [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) or [Opencode](https://opencode.ai/) installed, start either one in a secondary terminal, for example:

```shell
opencode
```

::: details Installing Claude Code or OpenCode ...

Install [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/), for example via npm:
```shell
npm install -global opencode-ai
```

Install [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview), for example via Homebrew:
```shell
brew install claude-code
```

Install [Claude Code for VSCode](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=anthropic.claude-code):
```shell
code --install-extension anthropic.claude-code
```

:::


![OpenCode started initially](opencode-start-screen.png){.ignore-dark}



Go ahead and interact with your CAP services using natural language and conversational style via OpenCode, entering prompts like these:

```sh
list books
```
```sh
order wuthering heights
```

And answer the questions that OpenCode asks you back.

![List books and ordering books via OpenCode](opencode-list-and-order-books.png){.ignore-dark}



You can also run `opencode web` to open the OpenCode web interface, which provides a more user-friendly way to interact with your MCP servers, including features like tool inspection and query building. Here's a screenshot of a simple session:

### Autowired MCP Clients

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#autowired-mcp-clients


When we initially started OpenCode above, it indicated in the bottom line of the interface that there's (at least) one MCP server connected.

![OpenCode status line showing connected MCP servers](opencode-status-line.png){.ignore-dark}

Enter `/status` in the OpenCode interface to see details, which should display the status of the connected MCP servers like this:

![OpenCode listing connected MCP servers](opencode-status.png){.ignore-dark}

> [!tip] Autowired during development
> Whenever you start your CAP application with `cds watch`, all served MCP endpoints are automatically registered with local MCP clients like [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs) and [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/), so you can just go ahead and run queries from them without any additional configuration. This makes it super easy to test and interact with your services via MCP during development.

::: details Click to expand the client-specific configuration files
::: code-group
```json [~/.claude.json]
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cds:AdminService": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://localhost:4004/mcp/admin",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Basic YWxpY2U6"
      }
    },
    "cds:CatalogService": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://localhost:4004/mcp/browse",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Basic YWxpY2U6"
      }
    }
  },
}
```
```json [~/.config/opencode/opencode.json]
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "cds:AdminService": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "http://localhost:4004/mcp/admin",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Basic YWxpY2U6"
      },
      "enabled": true
    },
    "cds:CatalogService": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "http://localhost:4004/mcp/browse",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Basic YWxpY2U6"
      },
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```
:::




### Inspect Log Output

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#inspect-log-output


When you run queries, you can inspect the log output of your CAP server to see the incoming MCP requests and how they are processed. This can be helpful for debugging and understanding the interaction between the MCP client and your CAP services.

For example, for a `list books` prompt, you should see log output similar to this:

::: code-group
```js [Node.js]
[mcp] - CatalogService describe { entities: [ 'Books' ] }
[mcp] - CatalogService query {
  cql: 'SELECT ID, title, author, genre, stock, price, currency_code FROM Books'
}
```
```js [Java]
INFO com.sap.cds.adapter.mcp.McpServlet : Received MCP query request for entity 'Books' with select fields [ID, title, author.name, genre.name, stock, price] and limit 20
```
:::


## Served out of the box

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#served-out-of-the-box


The adapter creates an MCP server per CAP service, hence each CAP application can expose multiple MCP servers. By default, the adapter creates three generic tools, [`describe`](#-describe-service), [`query`](#-query-entity), and [`call`](#-call-action), for each MCP server, which can be used by LLMs and AI agents to interact with the service.

the following tools for each MCP server, which can be used by LLMs and AI agents to interact with the service.

> [!warning]
> Tools are meant to be used by LLMs and AI agents and do not constitute a stable API.
> They may change in the future based on the needs of LLMs and AI agents. For stable APIs, please use the existing CAP protocols like OData, REST, GraphQL, etc.

### • `describe` service

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#-describe-service


This tool returns information about the entities and their elements exposed by the service. It also returns information about unbound actions and functions. If you do not provide a parameter, the tool describes all exposed entities, actions and functions. The optional parameter `entity` restricts the output to a single entity, the optional parameter `action` restricts the output to a single action/function. The tool provides an enum that lists all available entities, actions and functions.

### • `query` entity

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#-query-entity


This tool is used to read data from the service.
It expects a single parameter `cql`, which contains the query in [CQL](../../cds/cql) syntax to be executed.

> [!tip] CQL = SQL++ => well understood by LLMs
> As common LLMs, like Claude Sonnet, are trained for SQL very well, they are quick to understand and generate CQL queries for interacting with the service.

For example, given the `BookshopService` as [declared above](#mcp-specific-services) that exposes `Authors` with its to-many association to `Books` , we can ask OpenCode running Opus something like this:

```sh
list authors with their written books and genres
```

Which it would nicely translate into the following CQL query using nested postfix projection to expand the `books` association, as shown in the screenshot below:

```sql
SELECT from Authors {
  ID, name, books {
    title, genre
  }
}
```

![CQL query result showing authors with their written books and genres](cql-by-claude-opus.png){.ignore-dark}

### • `call` action

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#-call-action


This tool is used to call unbound actions or functions. The required parameter `action` is an enum that lists all unbound actions and functions exposed by the service. The parameters of the action or function to call can be provided via the optional parameter `parameters`, that must contain all required parameters of the action or function. The tool takes these parameters and calls the action or function on the service.

### Inspect the Tools

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#inspect-the-tools


You can use the [MCP Inspector](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/tools/inspector) to inspect the tools served from CAP services:

```bash
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector
```

The inspector should automatically open in your browser.

![MCP Inspector start page](mcp-inspector.png){.ignore-dark}

Register your `@mcp`-enabled CAP services to the inspector using the _Add Servers_ \> _+ Add manually_ menu option, and in the dialog that appears, follow these steps:

1. Enter a name for your server, e.g. _bookshop_.
1. Select _streamable-http_ as transport type.
3. Enter MCP endpoint into URL - for example, `http://localhost:4004/mcp/browse`.

A screenshot is shown below:

![MCP Inspector](mcp-inspector-add-server.png){.ignore-dark}

Then connect, and switch to the _Tools_ tab to the top of the inspector's window to inspect and try out the listed tools.


## Configuration

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#configuration


### Tool Name Prefixes

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#tool-name-prefixes


Some MCP clients or harnesses require unique tool names across all MCP servers. You can use the option <Config>cds.mcp.prefix</Config> to specify a prefix for the tool names. For example:

::: code-group
```yaml [.cdsrc.yaml]
cds:
  mcp:
    prefix: {service.name}-
```
```json [package.json]
{
  "cds": {
    "mcp": {
      "prefix": "{service.name}-"
    }
  }
}
```
:::

With this, the tool names generated by the MCP clients will be prefixed with the specified value, with the placeholder `{service.name}` being replaced by the actual service's fully qualified name – e.g., `CatalogService-describe`.


### Opting out of Autowiring

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#opting-out-of-autowiring


You can opt out of [autowired MCP clients](#autowired-mcp-clients) in development by setting the `cds.mcp.autowire` option to `false`, like so in your `package.json`:

::: code-group
```yaml [.cdsrc.yaml]
cds:
  mcp:
    autowire: false
```
```json [package.json]
{
  "cds": {
    "mcp": {
      "autowire": false
    }
  }
}
```
:::


### Mock Authentication

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#mock-authentication


[Autowired MCP clients](#autowired-mcp-clients) automatically add `Authorization` headers for the mock user `alice` (Node.js) or `privileged` (Java). If your service requires something different, you can customize the credentials via the `cds.mcp.autowire` configuration:

::: code-group
```yaml [.cdsrc.yaml]
cds:
  mcp:
    autowire:
      user: admin
      password: admin
```
```json [package.json]
{
  "cds": {
    "mcp": {
      "autowire": {
        "user": "admin",
        "password": "admin"
      }
    }
  }
}
```
:::

## Current Limitations

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#current-limitations


### Authorization with XSUAA

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#authorization-with-xsuaa


> [!important]
> We are currently working on providing out-of-the-box support for authorization with XSUAA, with PKCE, but it is not fully implemented yet.


### Query and Actions Only

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#query-and-actions-only


The MCP tools created by the adapter are currently focused on reading data and calling [**_unbound_** actions and functions](../../cds/cdl#actions) only. This means that you can use MCP to [`query`](#tool-query-entity) data from your CAP services, while any data changes need to be implemented via unbound actions for now.

For example, action `submitOrder` in the `CatalogService` ultimately creates an Order:

::: code-group
```cds [srv/catalog-service.cds]
service CatalogService {
  ...
  @requires: 'authenticated-user'
  action submitOrder ( book: Books:ID, quantity: Integer ); // [!code focus]
}
```
:::

Future versions of the adapter may add support for data changes using CREATE, UPDATE, and DELETE operations.


### Prompt Injection Attacks

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#prompt-injection-attacks


> [!caution]
> The MCP adapter does not perform any input validation or output validation to prevent prompt injection attacks.
> Agents can potentially be manipulated by data returned from the service to execute unintended actions. For any deployment ensure you use infrastructure and practices that mitigate prompt injection risks and connect only to trusted MCP agents (e.g., Joule).


## SAP API Policy

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/mcp#sap-api-policy


> [!caution]
> The adapter itself does not provide any built-in governance features: there is no automatic rate limiting, no specific audit logging of agent actions, no approval workflows for sensitive operations, and no policy enforcement layer. Before using MCP in a productive environment, put appropriate controls for example by using MCP Gateway of SAP Integration Suite or integrate with SAP Agent Gateway (not GA yet).

> [!caution]
> The CAP MCP adapter must not be used as a gateway or proxy for SAP Application APIs. The adapter is not an SAP-endorsed architecture, data service, or service-specific pathway under section 2.2.2 of the [_SAP API Policy_](https://help.sap.com/docs/business-accelerator-hub/sap-business-accelerator-hub/sap-api-policy) and is not an endorsed mechanism for exposing, proxying, or providing agentic access to SAP Application APIs.
> Any use of SAP Application APIs must be in accordance with the [_SAP API Policy_](https://help.sap.com/docs/business-accelerator-hub/sap-business-accelerator-hub/sap-api-policy). For SAP-endorsed patterns on agentic access to SAP Application APIs, consult the [_SAP Architecture Center_](https://architecture.learning.sap.com/docs/ref-arch/98efa0) reference architectures.

# CAP-level Agents

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/agents


CDS plugin for building agents based on the [A2A protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org).
{.abstract}

## Add the Agents Plugin

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/agents#add-the-agents-plugin


Within your project root run this to add the [`@cap-js/agents`](https://github.com/cap-js/agents) plugin:

```bash
npm add @cap-js/agents
```


## Declare `@agent` Services

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/agents#declare-agent-services



### Using `@agent` Annotation

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/agents#using-agent-annotation


Simply add the `@agent` annotation to a service definition to create an agent. For example, clone the [_capire/bookshop_](https://github.com/capire/bookshop) sample, and add a new file `srv/cat-service-agent.cds` with the following content:

::: code-group
```cds [srv/cat-service-agent.cds]
using { CatalogService  } from './cat-service';
annotate CatalogService with @agent;
```
:::

With that, the plugin auto-generates [MCP tools](./mcp) from the service's entities and actions, creates a [ReAct](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629) loop, and serves it via [A2A protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org) — no code required.


### Human-in-the-Loop

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/agents#human-in-the-loop


Annotate a CDS **action** with `@agent.hitl` to require human approval before the agent may execute it. For example, the `submitOrder` action in the `CatalogService` can be annotated like this:

::: code-group
```cds [srv/cat-service-agent.cds]
using { CatalogService  } from './cat-service';
annotate CatalogService with @agent;
annotate CatalogService.submitOrder with @agent.hitl; // [!code focus]
```
:::


When the agent decides to call the action, the task pauses and transitions to the A2A [`input-required`](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/#413-taskstate) state instead of running the action immediately.


## Test-drive Locally

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/agents#test-drive-locally



### Run with `cds watch`

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/agents#run-with-cds-watch


Start your server with `cds watch`, and note that the `@agent`-annotated service gets served with an additional endpoint for the A2A protocol:

```shell
cds watch
```
```shell
[cds] - serving CatalogService {
  at: [ ..., '/a2a/browse' ]
  ...
}
```

### Connect an LLM

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/agents#connect-an-llm


By default, the plugin uses a mock LLM for local development. Assuming you already have an LLM configured with a local installation of [Claude Code](https://claude.ai) or [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai), you can use that by simply adding this configuration:

::: code-group
```yaml [.cdsrc.yaml]
cds:
  requires:
    llm: anthropic
```
```jsonc [package.json]
"cds": {
  "requires": {
    "llm": "anthropic"
  }
}
```
:::


### Using Chat Preview

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/agents#using-chat-preview


For local development, the plugin serves a chat preview at http://localhost:4004/a2a/browse/preview/.



![alt text](chat-preview.png)




## Markdown-Based Agents

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/agents#markdown-based-agents


In addition you can further customize the agent by providing a Markdown-based agent definition, as described in the [Markdown-Based Agents](#markdown-based-agents) section.

### Markdown-Based Agents

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/agents#markdown-based-agents-1


To define an agent's identity, behaviour, and skills explicitly, add a sibling directory matching the slugified service name. When present, it replaces the default agentification: instead of the auto-generated ReAct agent, the plugin auto-builds the agent from the directory at startup — no JavaScript handler required.

```zsh
srv/
├─ travel-agent/.cds
└─ catalog-agent/                ← matches the slugified service name
   ├─ AGENTS.md                  ← agent identity + behaviour
   └─ skills/
      └─ book-purchase/
         └─ SKILL.md             ← workflow + examples
```

`AGENTS.md` defines who the agent is. The frontmatter populates the agent card;
the body is the agent's system prompt:

```md
---
name: catalog-agent
version: "1.0.0"
description: >
  Bookshop assistant for placing book orders on behalf of the user.
---

# Catalog Agent

## Identity

You are the **Catalog Agent**, a helpful assistant for the capire bookshop.
...
```


## Configuration

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/agents#configuration


### LLM Configuration

> Source: /docs/guides/ai/agents#llm-configuration


The LLM used by an agent is configured via `cds.requires.llm`. You can provide a `kind` as with [any required service](https://cap.cloud.sap/docs/node.js/core-services#required-services).

::: code-group
```yaml [.cdsrc.yaml]
cds:
  requires:
    llm:
      kind: aicore
      model: anthropic--claude-4.6-sonnet
```
```jsonc [package.json]
"cds": {
  "requires": {
    "llm": {
      "kind": "aicore",
      "model": "anthropic--claude-4.6-sonnet"
    }
  }
}
```
:::


| Kind     | Description                                                           |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `aicore` | The default for `production` and `hybrid`, connects to SAP AI Core    |
| `mock`   | The default for `development`, provides a mocked response when called |
| `anthropic` | Alternative for `development`, fetching credentials from local Claude or OpenCode installations |

See [SAP AI Core → Create a Service Instance](https://help.sap.com/docs/sap-ai-core/sap-ai-core-service-guide/create-service-instance) for how to create an instance.
